question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=3x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $\pi /12$ | $\pi /9$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\pi /4$ | $\pi /3$ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /12}^{\pi /9}6\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}6\operatorname{sec}⁡(u)\operatorname{tan}⁡(u)\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sec}⁡(u)\operatorname{tan}⁡(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{sec}⁡(u){|}_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3} \\  & =2(\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =2(2-\sqrt{2}) \\  & =4-2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$
